guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: During the third quarter, Boyd continued to outperform the underlying industry volume and gain market share, supported by its scale and ongoing market densification strategy. Volume gains driven by the strength of the company’s performance and insurer relationships contributed to positive same-store sales growth during the quarter of 2.2%, complemented by a modest increase in total cost of repair.
Boyd estimates repairable claims volumes declined approximately 1–3% year-over-year in Q3 2026, which is consistent with our long-term planning assumptions.

In October 2026, same-store sales growth continued to be positive. Given the inherent monthly and quarterly variability, the Company evaluates same-store sales over longer periods and does not view any single period as indicative of sustainable market share expansion or multi-year strategic targets.

Project 360 and acquisition synergies are on track to deliver a further $15 million in the fourth quarter, elevating total projected savings to $65 million for 2026 and $140 million across the 2025–2029 period.

During the quarter, Boyd announced a normal course issuer bid and commenced share repurchases under the program. This initiative reflects our commitment to disciplined, returns-focused capital allocation. Boyd’s objective is to ensure that capital is consistently directed toward high risk-adjusted return opportunities, whether through growth investments in strategic or single-shop acquisitions, brownfield and greenfield start-up locations, investments in existing operations, debt reduction, share repurchases, dividends or other alternatives.
The Company expects to complete and open 11 start-up locations in the fourth quarter.
